panels.headline: Addressing knowledge insufficiency in extended reasoning chains
content: LRMs excel in long stepwise reasoning through large-scale reinforcement learning.
Extended reasoning processes face knowledge gaps, leading to uncertainties and errors.
Automating knowledge supplementation is crucial for enhancing reasoning reliability.
Search-o1 aims to integrate agentic search into LRM reasoning to improve performance.
This work targets complex reasoning tasks in science, mathematics, and coding.

panels.headline: Overthinking and knowledge gaps in extended reasoning chains
content: Extended reasoning chains in LRMs can cause overthinking and increased risks of knowledge gaps.
These issues can propagate errors and disrupt the reasoning process.
Manual verification of complex reasoning problems is costly and time-consuming.
Automating the supplementation of knowledge is a significant challenge.
Search-o1 addresses these challenges by integrating agentic search into the reasoning process.

panels.headline: Integrating agentic RAG and Reason-in-Documents
content: Search-o1 combines an agentic RAG mechanism with a Reason-in-Documents module.
The agentic RAG mechanism dynamically retrieves external knowledge for uncertain points.
The Reason-in-Documents module analyzes and refines retrieved documents to maintain coherent reasoning.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of reasoning approaches: (a) Direct reasoning without retrieval often results in inaccuracies due to missing knowledge. (b) Our agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning approach improves knowledge access but usually returns lengthy, redundant documents, disrupting coherent reasoning.

panels.headline: Pass@1 metric on PhD-level science QA, math, and code benchmarks
content: Search-o1 was tested on complex reasoning tasks in science, mathematics, and coding.
It achieved significant improvements in reasoning performance and general knowledge.
Quantitative analysis confirmed its efficiency and scalability.
panels.figure_caption: Main results on challenging reasoning tasks, including PhD-level science QA, math, and code benchmarks. We report Pass@1 metric for all tasks. For models with 32B parameters, the best results are in bold and the second-best are underlined. Results from larger or non-proprietary models are in gray color for reference.

panels.headline: Search-o1 outperforms direct reasoning in complex tasks
content: Search-o1 significantly reduces reasoning uncertainties and errors.
It demonstrates substantial improvements in reasoning performance and general knowledge.
The framework is efficient and scalable, suitable for various reasoning domains.
Performance is validated across five complex reasoning domains and six open-domain QA benchmarks.

panels.headline: Enhancing LRMs with agentic search for reliable reasoning
content: Search-o1 enhances the trustworthiness and applicability of LRMs in complex reasoning tasks.
It paves the way for more reliable and versatile intelligent systems.
The framework addresses key challenges in extended reasoning chains, such as overthinking and knowledge gaps.
Future work will focus on further optimizing the agentic RAG mechanism and Reason-in-Documents module.
Search-o1 has the potential to revolutionize reasoning in LRMs by integrating external knowledge effectively.
